title: With a start picture, prompt only the change
rule: When the generator gets a start picture, write only what moves and what the camera does, and do not redescribe what the picture already shows.
why: The picture fixes subject, composition and light; extra description can reduce motion or contradict the picture, and several vendors say to delete sentences that only describe the scene.
how: Replace 'a woman in a red coat stands in a rainy street' with 'she turns toward the camera; slow push-in; rain keeps falling'.

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js composeClip (film.pictures drops the character description but 'It begins like this' and Look lines still describe the scene)
monofilm.idea: Add a motion-only prompt variant per generator (flag image_first in GENERATORS) that keeps only beat, move, camera, timing and dialogue.

title: State what must hold still in positive words
rule: Say what stays still or unchanged in positive terms (the camera holds completely still, the room stays the same) instead of a list of 'no' phrases.
why: Runway's guidance says negated phrasing can backfire and the model reads what should happen; the Runway docs show the positive form for holding the camera.
how: 'The camera holds completely still. Only the steam moves.'

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js composeClip ('No scene change, no cuts, no text on screen', 'Do not repeat it', timingLine)
monofilm.idea: Rewrite the fixed clauses as positive statements ('one continuous shot, the text-free frame') for generators flagged no-negation.

title: Fill a negative-prompt field with nouns, not instructions
rule: Where a generator has a negative-prompt field, list unwanted things as plain nouns and not as 'no X' or 'don't X' sentences.
why: Google's Veo guide says to list elements (wall, frame) rather than write 'no walls'; instruction words in the field work worse.
how: negative: 'urban background, man-made structures, text, watermark'

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js composeClip builds negative from film.never and look.forbidden prefixed 'no ' (never.map(no ...)); forGenerator
monofilm.idea: Strip the leading 'no ' from forbidden terms when the generator has a real negative field; keep the sentence form only for the folded 'Do not show' fallback.

title: Keep a per-generator capability profile
rule: Keep one record per generator listing input types, max seconds, resolutions, negative-prompt support, reference limits, seed support and prompt length, and make the export use it.
why: These differ widely: Runway has no usable negation and a 1000 character prompt, Hailuo allows 2000 characters, Wan has a negative field and about 5s, Sora allowed two characters and up to 20s.
how: Fields: negative, end_picture, native_audio, max_seconds, max_chars, max_refs, sizes, seed, rewrites_prompt.

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js GENERATORS (negative, end_picture, native_audio, max_seconds, notes) for minimax-h3 and generic only
monofilm.idea: Add max_chars, max_refs, sizes, seed and rewrites_prompt, and profiles for the commonly used generators (see docs/knowledge/models).

title: One shot, one subject action, one camera move per clip
rule: Write each clip prompt as a single shot with one main action and one camera move.
why: OpenAI, Hailuo, Kling and Runway guides all name stacked actions and competing camera moves as the main cause of ignored or muddled instructions.
how: 'Slow push-in on the girl as she lifts the lid and smells the soup.'

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js composeClip ('Camera: oneMove(n.cam), one continuous shot'; beats per clip)

title: Shorter clips obey better
rule: Plan clips of 4 to 6 seconds when the end picture or a precise action must be hit, and join them in the edit.
why: OpenAI says short clips follow instructions more reliably and two 4s clips can beat one 8s; a Veo guide says 4s clips hit the end frame more tightly than 8s; Kling guide says test at 5s first.
how: Split a 10s scene into two 5s clips with a start picture each.

monofilm.idea: Let the plan prefer 4-6s clips for scenes with an end picture; make the target length a per-generator setting.

title: Treat the end frame as a guide
rule: Do not rely on an end picture being hit exactly; ask for it on the last frame and check the returned clip against it.
why: A Veo guide reports the first frame is followed closely and the last only loosely, tighter for 4s clips; Monofilm's own generator notes say clips reach the end early and then hold still.
how: Prompt: 'reach the end picture on the very last frame' and measure the stand-still time.

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js timingLine; src/takereview.js (frames judged against the start and end pictures); hold and cuts measures in src/mcp-video.js

title: Dialogue goes in its own block and stays short
rule: Put spoken lines in a separate block after the scene description, one or two short lines per 4 seconds.
why: OpenAI says long speeches sync poorly and a 4s shot fits one or two short exchanges; Google says to describe audio in sentences separate from visuals.
how: 'Dialogue: Mimi says, "Look, it grew!"'

monofilm.idea: Warn at planning time when a clip's lines exceed about 2 short sentences per 4 seconds.

title: Describe sound in separate sentences and say if you want none
rule: State the audio wish explicitly (sound effects, ambience, dialogue or none) in sentences apart from the picture description.
why: Google's Veo guide asks to state whether audio is wanted and to separate it from the visuals; without it, models invent music.
how: 'Audio: only the ambient sound described above. No speech, no music.'

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js AUDIO_TEXT and composeClip Sound/Dialogue parts

title: Name the character in the prompt when using character or reference slots
rule: When the generator holds a reference or stored character, call that character by its name or tag in the prompt.
why: OpenAI says the id alone is not enough and the name must appear; Runway lets a tag be mentioned with at-syntax.
how: '@Mimi opens the door' or 'Mimi opens the door' when Mimi is the stored character name.

monofilm.idea: Emit the generator's own tag syntax for each reference when the generator profile has one.

title: Respect the reference-picture cap
rule: Send no more reference pictures than the generator documents (Sora 2 two characters, Veo about three, Omni Flash six) and prefer one character plus one setting.
why: Beyond the cap uploads are dropped or the model blends them; a Veo guide calls three the practical ceiling.
how: For a two-character scene send two character references and let the start picture carry the place.

monofilm.idea: Add max_refs to GENERATORS and have the pack choose the most important references when a scene has more.

title: Match the start and end pictures to the output size
rule: Give the generator start and end pictures at exactly the output aspect ratio and size.
why: Sora requires input_reference to match the size; Veo and Runway guides warn that mismatched ratios cause crops, stretching or bars; Hailuo accepts only ratios 2:5 to 5:2.
how: Draw the pictures at the film aspect ratio and crop never after the fact.

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js composeClip (look.aspect) and picture drawing in src/wizard.js makeFrame
monofilm.idea: Check picture dimensions against the chosen generator's sizes in the pack step.

title: Use the generator's own camera words
rule: Write the camera move with the generator's documented vocabulary, one move per bracket or phrase.
why: Hailuo has 15 bracketed commands, Luma publishes a list of camera strings, Higgsfield uses named presets; unlisted wording gives less accurate moves.
how: Hailuo: '[Push in] ...'. Luma: ask the concepts endpoint for the string.

monofilm.idea: Map the planner's camera field to a vocabulary table per generator in GENERATORS.

title: Keep the prompt inside the generator's length range
rule: Cut the clip prompt to the generator's length: Runway motion prompt 1 to 1000 characters, Hailuo 2000 characters, LTX under 200 words, Wan about 80-120 words, Kling about 50-100 words.
why: Text past the limit is rejected or ignored, and guides tie quality to compact prompts.
how: Drop fixed boilerplate before story content when over the limit.

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js composeClip builds a long multi-line prompt with no length check
monofilm.idea: Add max_chars per generator, and a compact variant that keeps beat, camera, dialogue and timing first.

title: Know whether the generator rewrites your prompt
rule: Record whether the generator rewrites or extends the prompt, and switch it off when the wording is exact canon.
why: Hailuo's optimizer is on by default and expands loose prompts, Wan recommends extension, Hunyuan's Master rewrite can drop semantic detail.
how: Hailuo: turn the optimizer off when exact bracket commands or object constraints are in the prompt.

monofilm.idea: Add rewrites_prompt to the generator profile and show a hint in the pack when it is on.

title: Show emotion as action, not as a label
rule: Describe the visible change in performance and do not write 'she is sad' or stack several emotions in one clip.
why: Hailuo and LTX guides both advise physical reactions over emotion words; one expression change per close-up.
how: 'Her smile fades and her eyes drop to the floor.'

monofilm.idea: Add a line to the scene-writing instructions in src/wizard.js SCENES_SYSTEM and check beats for bare emotion words.

title: Change one variable per retry and keep the seed
rule: When a take fails, change one thing in the prompt or picture per retry, record the seed, and expect similar rather than identical results from a fixed seed.
why: Runway and OpenAI guides advise simplifying and changing one variable; a fixed seed helps explore similar motion but is not identical.
how: Retry with the same seed and one edited clause, or a new seed and the same prompt, not both.

monofilm.where: src/mcp-video.js (retry.seed, retry.add_to_prompt, seed saved with each take)

title: Multi-shot in one prompt only for generators that support it
rule: Describe several shots in one prompt only for generators with native multi-shot or timestamp prompting; otherwise give one shot per clip.
why: Veo supports timestamp segments and Seedance claims native multi-shot, but Runway guidance says combined scenes compete, and Monofilm's notes say MiniMax H3 cuts when several shots are listed.

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js composeClip ('one continuous shot', 'No scene change, no cuts'); GENERATORS minimax-h3 note

title: Concrete visible details, not style words
rule: Replace vague cues (cinematic, beautiful, moves quickly) with visible, checkable details and a few colour anchors.
why: OpenAI says vague cues do little; LTX warns about flicker from unclear lighting; Kling guide lists no lighting plan as a pitfall.
how: 'wet asphalt, neon reflections, three colours: teal, amber, black'

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js composeClip Look line (look.look or look.base)
monofilm.idea: Have the look generator output 3 to 5 concrete colour/lighting anchors and put them in the Look line.

title: Give pacing words and match the motion to the image
rule: Include pacing words (slow, subtle, continuous) and only request motion the picture can support.
why: Runway docs: without pacing words motion is average; asking a head-and-shoulders shot to walk away or adding off-frame elements fails.
how: 'slow, steady drift; she stays at the table'

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js timingLine (full length, slow steady movement)
monofilm.idea: Check each beat against the start picture's framing during planning (no walking from a close-up).

title: Mind content filters and rights
rule: Keep prompts and input pictures inside the generator's content rules (no real people or faces as input for Sora, no copyrighted characters, under-18 suitable) and have a plan for refusals.
why: OpenAI rejected real people, face images and copyrighted characters; Google blocks content that violates its policies and warns about horror content.
how: If a clip is refused, retry without the never-show clause, then with shortened sentences.

monofilm.where: Content-filter retry commit e1f1805 (refusal retry without the never-show clause, then shortened sentences)

title: Expect generators to be retired
rule: Do not hard-code one generator: keep the generator list editable and dated, and re-check availability before a production.
why: In 2026 the Sora 2 API was shut down (24 Sep) and the Veo 3.1 preview models in the Gemini API were shut down (22 Oct); Moonvalley's API and some LTX/Kling versions were also retired.
how: Store generator id, version and a last-verified date.

monofilm.idea: Add version and verified-date fields and an 'unavailable' state.

title: Export to valid sizes and frame counts on local models
rule: For open models, export at the sizes and frame counts the model supports (LTX width/height divisible by 32 and 8k+1 frames; Hunyuan 129 frames; Wan TI2V 1280x704; Mochi 480p).
why: Other values are padded, cropped or degrade quality.
how: LTX: 121 frames is 8x15+1; 257 max recommended.

monofilm.idea: Add sizes and frame-rule fields to the profile of each local generator.

title: Prefer one subject plus one setting, and few ideas
rule: Limit a clip to a small number of ideas (2 to 4) with one hero subject.
why: Kling guides say too many ideas overwhelm the model; Wan guide says overloaded prompts hurt.
how: Move extra business into the next clip.

monofilm.idea: Add a planner check that flags a beat with more than one action or more than four named things.
